title: Unaware, Unfunded, Untrained and Unsupported: A Systematic Review of SME Cybersecurity
extended_summary:
This paper is not the requested secondary-students AI writing study. Instead, it is a systematic review of cybersecurity research on small and medium enterprises (SMEs). The review addresses five main questions: what cyber threats SMEs experience, what awareness SMEs have of those threats, what cybersecurity controls they adopt, what frameworks apply to SMEs, and what barriers SMEs face in becoming cyber resilient. The authors argue that SMEs are economically important yet consistently underserved in cybersecurity research and practice.

The study uses a systematic review approach following PRISMA-P and Cochrane guidance. Searches were conducted across ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, ProQuest, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language studies published from 2017 onward. From 1,090 records, the authors screened and narrowed the evidence base to 132 included studies. They extracted information on publication year, theme, study type, data collection method, sample size, geographic coverage, frameworks discussed, motivations, conclusions, recommendations, and limitations. The synthesis combined content analysis and thematic analysis, and also included a "systematic knowledge gap analysis" distinguishing themes used merely to motivate papers from themes empirically tested in the literature.

The population studied is SMEs and the reviewed literature about them, not students, teachers, or schools. The context is organisational cybersecurity across multiple countries and regions, with some attention to differences between developed and developing countries. The review reports that many included studies were qualitative, that only a small number used substantial quantitative analysis, and that a meaningful share of the literature focused on proposed interventions or frameworks rather than strong empirical testing.

The main conclusions are that SME cybersecurity research is still shallow and repetitive, with limited cumulative empirical progress. Across the literature, the most recurring barriers to cyber resilience are lack of awareness of cybersecurity risks, limited cybersecurity literacy, and underfunded or resource-constrained security programs. The review also finds that available frameworks and solutions are often poorly tailored to SME needs, and suggests that limited cybersecurity literacy may be a root cause underlying both awareness and resource-allocation problems.
quality_tier_rationale: The provided paper is a systematic review of SME cybersecurity, not an education study and not an evaluation of any AI or educational technology intervention. It contains no K-12 learner sample, no writing intervention, and no education-relevant causal or comparative evidence for the target topic.
impact_tier_rationale: Because this paper does not study an educational intervention or learner outcomes, there is no evidence of impact on student writing, school operations, or educational systems relevant to the requested 2025 secondary-writing AI study.
